# Pinned + hashed blake3 for the independent artifact re-hash in action.yml.
# That step is the ONLY integrity check that runs on a cache hit, so an
# unpinned `pip install blake3` would let a hijacked release decide whether a
# poisoned artifact ships. Installed with --require-hashes --only-binary=:all:,
# so pip refuses anything whose sha256 isn't listed below.
#
# Hashes are PyPI's own, verbatim (pip download + pip hash / the PyPI JSON API).
# Every caller runs ubuntu-latest x86_64, so only the manylinux x86_64 wheels
# are listed; multiple --hash lines are OR'd, covering the CPython versions the
# runner image may ship. 3.12+ only on purpose: below that blake3 pulls in
# typing-extensions, which would need pinning too — a runner that old would
# fail loudly here rather than install something unverified.
#
# Bump: pip download blake3 --only-binary=:all: -d /tmp/dl && pip hash /tmp/dl/*
blake3==1.0.9 \
    --hash=sha256:bcd56a7a972c4185070f7042ccc20166927eec3c0f98b8405f375d007b604a0b \
    --hash=sha256:66c84dbc2a31eda88b55bbf5c5b711037bf0698eba0fd1faf06bdaf313c39048 \
    --hash=sha256:f65d77eb05331495485048f6804f53885b192b998acb7e6fe1487d941bf08435 \
    --hash=sha256:c7f648fa425138452d1e585ac625c7aefddb946d9765906c4c12d564a1523cd8
